note: BROU only, among the main banks: Itaú Uruguay's manual of rates and prices (version 1 October 2026) prices its cards' yearly charge in indexed units but states no card interest rate, so its cards can't be written; Santander Uruguay's site sits behind Incapsula and BBVA Uruguay's refused the request (403). Banco República's particular conditions for its Visa credit cards (conditions in force February 2025), read in full: the Internacional, Oro and Platino cards, each with its yearly charge with VAT (billed in three monthly instalments; issue costs nothing). The Internacional's charge is waived in full on average spending of 35,000 pesos a month the year before, written as 420,000 in the year, and the Platino's on 60,000 a month, written as 720,000 (the 50% discounts on lower averages are steps not written; the Oro's table gives only a half discount up to 35,000, not written). Balances and cash advances in pesos bear an effective 65.00% a year, and late balances the moratory 84.38%, written as the penalty rate. Purchases abroad on the Internacional carry 3% plus VAT (whose rate isn't stated), written as 3%; the Oro and Platino are exempt. Cash advances at BROU's own branches and network cost nothing. No minimum payment or grace period is stated.
